sender: Naomi Brandt, Cloud & Internet Channel Research, Calloway & Dunn Securities
subject: AMZN: AWS reseller/MSP billing panel points to Sept-quarter acceleration - we raise 3Q AWS rev to $41.5bn (Street ~$40.3bn)
body:
CALLOWAY & DUNN SECURITIES | Cloud Channel Checks | Oct 14

AMZN: AWS channel checks point to upside - raising 3Q AWS estimates, introducing 4Q view

What we did: We aggregated September billing data from 9 AWS resellers and managed service providers. Together they bill about $2.4bn annualized through AWS Marketplace and consolidated-billing arrangements. Two are large enough to be top-10 partners in North America. We compared Jul-Sep against Apr-Jun and against the year-ago quarter.

What we found:
- Panel billings: +26% y/y in the Sept quarter, vs. +21% in June. The acceleration was broad and not driven by one customer.
- Mix: GPU/accelerator instance and inference-related spend (managed model endpoints, vector database, data pipeline) rose from 14% of panel billings to 19% in the quarter. Core compute and storage grew +18% y/y, up from +16%.
- Commitments: Four of the nine partners report average enterprise commit size up 12-20% on renewals. They attribute this to AI workloads moving from pilot to production. None reported commit downsizing at scale.
- Capacity: Three partners said they were told to expect GPU instance wait times through December. This looks like a supply limit, not a demand one.

Estimate changes (preliminary):
- 3Q26 AWS revenue to $41.5bn (+25.8% y/y) from $40.1bn. Consensus is ~$40.3bn (+22.1%).
- AWS operating margin 3Q to 34.4% from 35.2%, on higher depreciation from the AI build and early Trainium ramp costs. Consensus is ~35.0%.
- 4Q AWS revenue to $44.8bn (Street ~$43.2bn).
- Consolidated 3Q operating income to $21.6bn (from $20.9bn). Consensus is ~$20.7bn.

Caveats: The panel is small relative to AWS ($130bn+ annualized) and skews toward mid-market and digitally native customers. Partner billing can lead or lag recognized revenue by up to a month, so treat this as direction, not a point estimate. We would not extrapolate the growth rate to large enterprise.

Bottom line: If AWS prints around +25%, it would be a 3-point beat on growth, partly offset by a margin shortfall vs. the Street. Rating Buy, PT $262 (from $255).

Naomi Brandt | Calloway & Dunn Securities
Full panel table and partner breakdown attached. Disclosures at callowaydunn.com/disclosures.
